stem: In formal written English, choose the quoted part that contains an error. Choose “No error” if every part is acceptable. Sentence: No one in the records unit were absent from Monday’s briefing.
explanation: No one is singular, so it takes was, not were, in this statement. The phrase in the records unit does not change the subject’s number. Corrected sentence: No one in the records unit was absent from Monday’s briefing.

stem: In formal written English, choose the quoted part that contains an error. Choose “No error” if every part is acceptable. Sentence: Both the coordinator and the volunteers checks the equipment before each drill.

choices.text: Both the coordinator and the volunteers

explanation: The subject joins the coordinator and the volunteers with both ... and, making it plural. Use check rather than checks: Both the coordinator and the volunteers check the equipment before each drill.

stem: In formal written English, choose the quoted part that contains an error. Choose “No error” if every part is acceptable. Sentence: The curator’s report includes photographs of the newly restored paintings.
explanation: There is no error. The singular noun report takes includes. Curator’s correctly marks one curator’s possession, photographs is the object, and newly correctly modifies restored. Do not change includes to include because paintings is not the subject.

stem: Choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. The volunteers labelled ___ equipment before lending it to the team.
explanation: Their is the possessive determiner showing whose equipment it is. They’re means they are, there indicates a place, and there’s means there is or there has. None can replace the possessive their here.

stem: Choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. The caretaker agreed ___ unlock the storage room at dawn.
explanation: Agreed is followed here by the to-infinitive: agreed to unlock. Too means also or excessively, two is a number, and then does not supply the required infinitive marker.

stem: Choose the phrasal verb that means postpone and correctly completes the sentence. Rather than continue with contaminated samples, the team decided to ___ the inspection until replacement samples arrived.
explanation: Put off means postpone, so it fits a decision to conduct the inspection later. Put out, put through, and put up have different meanings; they do not express postponing the inspection in this sentence.
